page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c9ae.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an AMD EPYC 9T95 processor using the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 96 dedicated vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 2.25 GHz, paired with 192.0 GB of system memory. This resource configuration yields a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, characteristic of compute-oriented cloud architectures. The instance includes a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth allocation, while featuring zero local storage and no hardware GPU accelerators.

Because the instance relies entirely on remote storage volumes and includes no integrated disk storage, operational deployments depend on external network-attached volumes. In terms of cost efficiency, the compute-heavy hardware profile minimizes memory overhead expenses for workloads that primarily demand parallel CPU cycles rather than large in-memory footprints. The 96 dedicated cores provide predictable execution without CPU contention, and the 50 Gbps network interface supports substantial data movement between compute workers and distributed services.

The resource balance of ecs.c9ae.24xlarge makes it targeted for highly parallel, compute-bound tasks that do not require massive per-core memory capacities or specialized GPU acceleration. Standard workloads include batch processing pipelines, video encoding, continuous integration and build automation, scientific compute models, distributed data processing, and front-end web serving clusters operating under sustained request volume.
